body:
AUDIT of #152/#153/#154 (2026-07-21), findings F2 + F3. My own T40 fix, reviewed. F2 CONFIRMED, F3 PLAUSIBLE.

**F2 — the VACUUM can make a store UN-OPENABLE.** `src/store/sqlite.ts:71-72` runs `VACUUM` in the CONSTRUCTOR when `freelist_count > 0`. VACUUM needs an exclusive write lock over the whole file. With a second handle holding a read transaction — the exact scenario the purge path 120 lines below probes and handles — it waits out `busy_timeout` and throws SYNCHRONOUSLY out of `new SqliteBackend(path)`. `src/cli/cli.ts:113, 217, 294, 385, 423` all construct it bare. **Before this change, opening a store took no exclusive lock at all.** The file's own header pins the contract this broke: WAL + busy_timeout is 'the multi-handle provision', and 'the methods are async so every failure arrives as a rejected promise'. The constructor is not async and has no guard. Secondary: VACUUM rewrites the entire file and needs ~2x its size free, so first open of a large store blocks for its full size on a path nothing treats as expensive.

FIX: wrap in try/catch. **The store must OPEN; the scrub is best-effort-and-REPORTED, not open-blocking.** Report the deferral rather than swallowing it (do not repeat H7 while fixing H7).

**F3 — the constructor VACUUM has no checkpoint.** In WAL mode VACUUM's rebuilt pages land in `store.db-wal`; the main file keeps the inherited plaintext freelist until a checkpoint folds it in. The purge path deliberately runs `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` AND checks `busy` for exactly this reason. The constructor does neither, so a process killed before `close()` leaves the store in §11 violation while the code believes it healed. FIX: follow the VACUUM with the same CHECKED checkpoint. PROBE to confirm: construct over a store with inherited freelist, do NOT close, then `strings store.db`.

P3/P4 (2026-07-24). Both findings PROBED LIVE at this revision before any code moved. F2 is real with one correction to its account: in WAL mode a READER does not block the VACUUM (probed — it lands in 3ms). A concurrent WRITER does: another handle holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` — which is what `append` holds — waits out `busy_timeout` and throws SQLITE_BUSY straight out of `new SqliteBackend(path)`. F3 is CONFIRMED as written: after the VACUUM and with no close, `store.db` still spells the erased row, and a checked `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` is what clears it. The reader's snapshot turns out to be exactly what refuses THAT checkpoint (`busy: 1`), so both findings have real, deterministic contention rails.

SHIPPED: the scrub is wrapped and its checkpoint is checked; a deferral is reported on two surfaces — an optional `onScrubDeferred` callback (wired to `io.err` at all five CLI store opens, through one `openStore` helper) and a `scrubDeferred` field for an embedder that never wired one. The callback itself is guarded: a reporter that throws (EPIPE on a closed stderr) must not re-wedge the open. Nothing is persisted — `freelist_count` is the durable to-do list, so an uncontended open retries.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, named in the rail file: a deferred scrub does NOT make byte-presence unprovable through `holds`. The inherited freelist belongs to erasures no surviving id names, so the only fail-closed answer is 'every id is unprovable', which would make one contended open refuse every erasure for the life of the process — a change to what the store promises rather than a repair of it. That is Myk's call, and it wants its own ticket if he wants it.

MUTATION PASS (adlc hollow-test, src/store/sqlite.ts). One survivor mattered: `freelist > 0` -> `freelist > 1` lived through the first three rails, because every fixture they build frees tens of pages. A store whose freelist holds exactly ONE page would have skipped the scrub with its plaintext legible — T72's 'the boundary is zero, not one' verbatim. Closed by a fourth rail over a fixture that sits ON the boundary: erase once, then keep appending, because the refills take freed pages back and one leftover page is the ordinary end state of that history. Watched RED against the mutant (`> 1`): the boundary rail alone fails, `expected true to be false` on the marker still legible in store.db; the other three stay green, which is exactly why they could not kill it. The remaining survivors are `busy_timeout 5000 -> 5001` and one cosmetic — config-constant mutations, accepted with reason, no rail owed.

FOUND WHILE BUILDING THAT FIXTURE, and NOT fixed here (P0 material): `freelist_count > 0` is a NECESSARY but not SUFFICIENT trigger. Probed — a legacy store whose later appends fully reclaimed the freed pages reads `freelist_count = 0` while the erased row's plaintext is still legible in store.db, on the reused pages' unwritten tails, and the scrub never fires: before, after open, and after close, the marker is there. So T71's one-time scrub under-detects, and this is not a contention story at all. Fixing it means either an unconditional VACUUM on every open of a store with no scrub watermark, or a durable 'scrubbed at version N' record — both decide something about cost and on-disk state rather than repairing a stated promise, so both want Myk.

P5 ERASURE LENS (independent, on this diff) — CONFIRMED a second path the `freelist_count` trigger cannot reach, a sibling of the reclaimed-page-tails finding above. A VACUUM COMMITS even under a concurrent reader (probed): the committed state then reads `freelist_count = 0` through the WAL while the rebuilt pages sit only in the `-wal` sidecar and the main file still spells the erased row. If the fold (the checked `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`) defers on that reader AND the process dies before any later checkpoint, the NEXT open reads `freelist_count = 0`, skips the whole scrub block, and `scrubDeferred` is undefined — a clean report over legible at-rest plaintext. Probed end-to-end: first open (reader present) commits + defers + reports; reader leaves; handle abandoned with no close; second uncontended open reads freelist 0, reports nothing, marker still in store.db.

REPAIRED IN THIS DIFF (a false statement, not a decision): the deferral message promised the plaintext stays 'until an uncontended open scrubs it', and the constructor comment called the freelist 'its own durable to-do list.' Both are true only for the VACUUM-REFUSED branch (freelist stays positive, self-heals) and false for the CHECKPOINT-DEFERRED branch (VACUUM committed, freelist reads 0, no re-trigger). The message now distinguishes the two branches and states the checkpoint-deferred one is not self-healing; the comment says the same.

NOT BUILT — joins the existing under-detection finding as evidence for the SAME (Myk) decision. Both the reclaimed-page-tails case (freelist reads 0 while reused pages' tails stay legible) and this checkpoint-crash case are unreachable by the `freelist_count > 0` trigger, so ONE fix closes both: a durable 'scrubbed at version N' watermark, or an unconditional checked `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on every open (folds a crashed scrub's surviving `-wal` frames in; no-op on an idle WAL) possibly paired with an unconditional-VACUUM-on-open watermark for the reclaimed-tails half. Either decides something about cost and on-disk state rather than repairing a stated promise — Myk's call. No rail is added for these here: a rail that needs a crash or a watermark to pass would assert the unbuilt decision, not the shipped behavior.
title: The sqlite constructor VACUUM can wedge a store closed, and may not reach the main file
